questions.prompt: Order the levels of organisation from smallest to largest.
questions.explain: Each level is made from the one below.
Blood is a tissue: a group of cells working together.

options: A group of similar cells working together to do a job
questions.explain: E.g. muscle tissue, nerve tissue, xylem in plants.

questions.prompt: Which is an organ in a plant?
questions.explain: A leaf contains several tissues working together.

questions.prompt: Explain why the stomach is called an organ and not a tissue.
questions.modelAnswer: The stomach is made of several different tissues working together: muscle tissue to churn food, gland tissue to make digestive juices, nerve tissue to control it, and lining tissue. A tissue is a group of similar cells doing one job, while an organ combines different tissues to carry out a bigger function (digesting food).
rubric: Named examples of tissues and their jobs

questions.prompt: Which are organ systems? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: The heart is an organ; muscle tissue is a tissue.

questions.prompt: An amoeba is a single cell. Which levels of organisation does it have?
questions.explain: In unicellular organisms, the one cell is the whole organism.

questions.text: Different tissues working together form an ___, and several of these working together form an organ ___.
questions.explain: Cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism.
